setlist.title: And We Bid You Good Night

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Victim Or The Crime** (2 reviews): A short Space appeared within it in the first set, signaling a trippy night to this attendee; The space section in Victim stirred strong memories for the reviewer [10][17]
- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodleloo** (1 review): Played very sweetly and quietly; the listener recalls the crowd so hushed a pin drop could be heard [10]
- **When I Paint My Masterpiece** (1 review): Reviewer found it nicely paced and well done [17]
- **Iko Iko** (1 review): The opening Drums, Iko and Women Smarter stretch gave parade marchers time to circle the Coliseum, yet was well played, aided by BeauSoleil's Michael Doucet [9]
- **Throwing Stones** (1 other source): A tape flip at its end was mended together at 9:20.593 [5]

## The recordings

- **gd90-02-27.sbd.ladner.8569.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 175 min; rated 3.67/5 by 27 [1]
- **gd1990-02-27.fob.senn421.alabamabob.andrewf.93955.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 21 songs; 160 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [5]
- **gd1990-02-27.141692.sbd.miller.flac1648**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 177 min [2]
- **gd1990-02-27.131005.cmc44.fob.mattes.katzeff.flac16**: audience recording; 20 songs; 180 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer was chosen via the Mardi Gras parade float contest, building a Berlin Wall float, to be dismantled during the parade, months after the wall fell [11]
- Healey and Michael Doucet added flavorful accents during the parade jam and Iko, which the band, especially Micky, fed off [12]
- Reviewer calls it the last great parking lot and Oakland Coliseum hotel scene, naming the Days Inn and Hampton Inn [13]
- Bill Walton rode a giant Chuck Taylor high top in the parade [17]
- Reviewer thinks the band may have briefly considered Lost Sailor just before going into Estimated [18]
- Michael Doucet and BeauSoleil joined for And We Bid You Good Night, and the Mardi Gras Parade cuts in, with minutes missing [5]
- Reviewer ranks it the best of the many Mardi Gras shows they attended, with a strong second set overall [9]
- Sound differs from spring tour and from 1989: laidback, lower energy, with plenty of open space for the music [13]
- Reviewer rates the whole three-night Mardi Gras run as well played, with a great atmosphere inside and outside [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd90-02-27.sbd.ladner.8569.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > DAT > CDR > WAV > SHNv3 [1]. Also: Reviewer's old Maxell 90-minute cassette copy possibly was cut at the same spot after Bird Song [14]
- **gd1990-02-27.fob.senn421.alabamabob.andrewf.93955.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Alabama Bob; transferred by Andrew F.; source: FOB AUD: Sennheiser MD-421's > Sony TC-D5M > TDK MA (1st Set), TDK MA-XG (2nd Set), with no Dolby. Mics on six-foot stand, at 90-degree spread, thirty feet… [5]. Also: Source tape was a MAC tape; the second-set disc break falls where it was flipped [5]
- **gd1990-02-27.141692.sbd.miller.flac1648**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Ultra Matrix SBD > Dat (48k) [2]
- **gd1990-02-27.131005.cmc44.fob.mattes.katzeff.flac16**: taped by Rick Katzeff and Ted Mattes; transferred by jwpetty; source: FOB Digital Audience Recording by Ted Mattes & Rick Katzeff using Schoeps CMC 44's> ? (presumed Oade p/s)> ? (presumed SV-250/255)> L. Deal clone; [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1990-02-27 Grateful Dead Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1990-02-27-grateful-dead-backstage-pass/) [21]
